en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on the Circular Path 7.
The Training Rule on Lowering the Eyes.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were walking through inhabited areas looking here and there... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall walk with downcast eyes while in an inhabited area.
One should walk in an inhabited area with downcast eyes, looking only a plough's length ahead."
If, out of disrespect, one walks through an inhabited area looking here and there, it is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is lacking mindfulness, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
